issues.description: Default speaker for bulbul:v3-beta contradicts documented contract (config sets 'shubh', docs say 'aditya')
issues.detail: Module docstring, class docstring, and PR description all declare 'aditya' as the v3-beta default, but TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS sets default_speaker='shubh'. Callers relying on the documented default will get a different voice. Pick one source of truth and make docs, PR text, and config agree.

issues.description: Pace silently clamped to model-specific subrange, violating the InputParams Field(ge=0.3, le=3.0) contract
issues.detail: Pydantic declares pace bounds 0.3-3.0, but __init__ silently clamps to 0.5-2.0 for v3-beta with only a warning. The precondition is stated twice and disagrees. Either raise ValueError on out-of-range pace (matching the strict STT discipline) or narrow the Field bounds per model. Pick one.

issues.description: Unsupported-parameter warnings compare against pydantic defaults, conflating 'unset' with 'explicitly set to default'
issues.detail: Code uses params.pitch != 0.0, params.loudness != 1.0, params.temperature != 0.6 to decide whether to warn. A caller passing the default value gets no warning; a caller who never touched the field is indistinguishable from one who set it explicitly. Use a None sentinel or model_fields_set so the invariant 'warn iff user supplied an unsupported parameter' holds.

issues.description: STT raises on unsupported params while TTS warns and drops them — inconsistent enforcement across the same package
issues.detail: SarvamSTTService raises ValueError on unsupported prompt/mode/language; SarvamHttpTTSService silently warns and drops pitch/loudness/temperature. Two services in the same module should not present opposite contracts for the same situation. Pick one substitution discipline (strict raise or documented best-effort) and apply it uniformly.

issues.description: get_speakers_for_model silently falls back to v2 speakers for unknown model names
issues.detail: The helper accepts an unconstrained str and returns v2 speakers on miss with no diagnostic. This masks caller errors and contradicts __init__, which raises ValueError on unknown models. Raise on unknown model or return an empty list — do not invent a default that looks plausible.

issues.description: Speaker enums and TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS.speakers tuples encode the same data twice
issues.detail: SarvamTTSSpeakerV2/V3 enums duplicate the speaker lists already in TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS. Dispatch keys on raw strings rather than the new SarvamTTSModel enum, so the enums are decorative and must be kept in sync manually. Pick one representation — either key configs by enum or drop the enums and let callers iterate the config.

synthesis.summary: The refactor to dataclass-driven model configs replaces fragile substring sniffing with a clean table-driven dispatch — the architectural direction is right. But the discipline is incomplete on the TTS side: the documented v3-beta default speaker ('aditya') disagrees with the config ('shubh'), pace bounds are stated twice and silently clamped rather than rejected, and the unsupported-parameter warnings compare against pydantic defaults so they fire by coincidence rather than by user intent. Enforcement policy also diverges from the STT module, which strictly raises. Fix the spec/code contradictions, pick a single substitution discipline across STT and TTS, and decide whether the new enums or the config tuples are the source of truth — the structure is sound, the details need to agree.
